history.summary: Major Shakti temple east of Ambikapur town dedicated to Goddess Mahamaya (Maa Ambika Bhawani); the city name Ambikapur is said to derive from goddess Ambika. Managed by the Sidh Shakti Peeth Shri Mahamaya Devi Mandir Trust. One travel portal claims it was erected in 1050 AD by Kalachuri king Ratansen, and a visitor review calls it a Shaktipeeth citing the Devi Bhagwat. CONFLICT FLAG: a local Hindi documentary says the present temple was constructed in 1910 (earlier the goddess sat on a simple chabutra) and credits the Singhdeo royal family with restoring scattered forest idols of the Surguja region — this contradicts the 1050 AD claim, so both dates need verification. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name; corrected to Chhattisgarh (state), town Ambikapur.

name: Mahamaya Temple
town_description: Ambikapur is the headquarters city of Surguja district in northern Chhattisgarh, a municipal centre and the main commercial hub of the Surguja region; its name is traditionally linked to the goddess Ambika (Mahamaya).

travel.airport: Maa Mahamaya Airport, Ambikapur (Darima, limited flights - verify); nearest major airport Raipur (~330 km, verify)
travel.road: Temple lies east of Ambikapur town; reachable by local taxi/auto

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Navratri and Durga Puja are the most festive periods
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning and evening aarti at 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM per one visitor review (verify locally)
